title: The Hart and the Hunter
summary: A stag, drinking at a woodland spring, gazed upon his reflection. He rejoiced in his grand, spreading antlers, but felt disgusted by his thin, spindly legs....
full_text:
A stag, drinking at a woodland spring, gazed upon his reflection. He rejoiced in his grand, spreading antlers, but felt disgusted by his thin, spindly legs.

Presently, a hunter appeared with arrows and hounds. The stag bounded away: his slender legs carried him across the open plain with breathless speed, saving him from the arrows.

Entering a dense thicket, his spreading horns became entangled in the brambles and branches. Held fast, the hounds overtook him.

As he fell beneath their claws, he cried: "Unhappy creature that I am! The legs I despised were my salvation, while the antlers I loved have brought my doom!"
moral: True value often lies in what is humble, while proud adornments bring peril.
